predecessors.name: Vijayanagara Empire
predecessors.text: Madurai and the other Tamil provinces Krishnadevaraya put under Viswanatha in 1529

successors.name: Carnatic Sultanate
successors.text: Tiruchirappalli, Madurai and Tinnevelly, held by Chanda Sahib from 1736

ledger.x: 1529: Krishnadevaraya makes Viswanatha Nayaka governor of Madurai.
1616: after the Battle of Toppur Muttu Virappa moves the capital from Madurai to Tiruchirappalli (infobox: Tiruchirapalli 1616-1634).
1634: the capital returns to Madurai under Tirumala Nayaka.

1635: Travancore resumes its tribute after Madurai attacks it (the page: Travancore resumed tribute after Madurai attacked it); the page also has Viswanatha helping Rama Raya's army subdue Travancore in 1544.
1673: Chokkanatha Nayaka of Madurai besieges Thanjavur and Vijaya Raghava, the last Nayak, falls in the battle.
Undated, placed 1673 (Chikka Devaraja's accession year, which is where Cliopatria's Mysore shape jumps): Coimbatore passes to Mysore.
1675: the Marathas under Venkoji take Thanjavur and Madurai's hold ends.
1695: the capital moves again to Tiruchirappalli (infobox 'Tiruchirapalli (1695-1716)'); the Rani Mangammal page has her capital at Tiruchy, undated.
1734: the Nawab of Arcot sends an expedition south against the Nayaks of Madurai (the page: the Nawab of Arcot sent a southern expedition in 1734).
1736: the fighting ends when Chanda Sahib is admitted into the Trichinopoly fort.
1736: Chanda Sahib takes Trichinopoly and the southern provinces.
1736: the Travancore tribute is taken to end with the dynasty.

wars.name: Mysore invasions of Madurai (1620-1625)
wars.outcome: Mysore invaded Dindigul in 1620 and was repelled; it invaded again in 1625 (around 1625 on the Thirumalai Nayak page, possibly instigated by Chamaraja Udaiyar); Harasura's advance toward Dindigul was beaten back by the Madurai general Ramaiyan and the Madurai…

wars.name: Mysore invasion of 1655
wars.outcome: Mysore invaded Madurai while Tirumala was ill; the page gives no outcome and no territorial change.

wars.name: Madurai's siege of Thanjavur
wars.outcome: Chokkanatha besieged Thanjavur in 1673 and Vijaya Raghava fell in the battle; Madurai held the city briefly until Venkoji took it in 1675.

wars.name: Chikka Devaraja's Trichinopoly campaign
wars.outcome: In 1696 Mysore attacked the Naiks of Madura and besieged Trichinopoly; 'the siege of Trichnopoly had to be abandoned because the alliance had begun to rupture' (no date).

wars.name: Nawab of Arcot's expedition and Chanda Sahib's takeover
wars.outcome: The Nawab of Arcot sent an expedition south in 1734; in 1736 Chanda Sahib entered the Trichinopoly fort and ended the Madurai Nayaks; the Marathas captured him there in 1741.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the extent is a list of districts (Coimbatore, Tirunelveli, Madurai, Aragalur) and the palayam system, and the Tirunelveli, Ramnad and Travancore edges are approximate throughout.
